items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I don’t know my Basie history as thoroughly as I should. In the ’50s the band was referred to as a polished, well-oiled machine... until Buck Clayton began to contribute, or Eddie Durham, or somebody.

ctx.x: I wish they could see your face. Say a triad again, and I’ll take a picture of it.

Triads [laughs]. I like the extensions and the alterations, whereas the earlier Basie band was highly improvisational, played a lot of head tunes, tunes that everybody just played from the head and didn’t have too much orchestration, written orchestration,

until Buck Clayton began to contribute, or Eddie Durham, or somebody. I don’t know my Basie history as thoroughly as I should. In the ’50s the band was referred to as a polished, well-oiled machine, not so highly improvisational as the earlier group, as the Old Testament, so to speak, band. The New Testament band was characterized mostly by heavy colors and textures in the orchestration, with the emphasis not particularly on the improvising solos, although there were excellent soloists in the New Testament…
